US secretary of state’s comments come as vulnerability in programming language Java highlighted
There is “zero evidence” that a wave of IT outages – which have grounded flights, cut off work access, limited bank access, affected Apple and disrupted classified communications – are related to each other or are the work of malign actors, according to the US secretary of state.
Marco Rubio said the US was “not under systemic attack” and a cascade of network problems was “not inter-related”.
In recent days, Microsoft , major US banks , Apple , American air traffic control systems and the National Security Agency have all been affected by technical failures and outages.
“We have zero evidence or any reason to believe that any of these isolated or individual instances have anything to do with nefarious actors, with cyber-hackers, with criminals, with another nation state, with a malign actor of any kind,” Rubio said.
Rubio’s comments came as cybersecurity researchers flagged a vulnerability in Java, a programming language used by 90% of companies in the Fortune 500, a ranking of the largest companies in the US. The researchers at US-based Calif used AI to discover the flaw and recently unearthed glitches in PHP, another computer language.
Calif said the Java flaw could allow hackers to remotely execute code, allowing them to place malicious software on a target’s systems.
The US director of national intelligence, Jay Clayton, said the incidents were caused by security upgrades – such as plugging the flaws in PHP – that took longer than planned or encountered unexpected hiccups.
“Everybody recognises it’s time to upgrade their systems, and as they upgrade them, they’re not coming back as expected in all cases, and in some cases, systems have to hand off to other systems, and those handoffs are not coming back as expected,” he told the Fox Business news channel.
Tal Be’ery, a cybersecurity expert, said he did not believe the incidents were linked directly but had a common underlying theme: AI. IT systems were buckling under the pressure of adding AI or tackling flaws uncovered by AI, he said.
“Our IT infrastructure is brittle, and when AI puts massive extra pressure on it, whether through upgrades to accommodate AI or through the rapid patching that AI-driven vulnerability discovery demands,” Be’ery said.
Since April, when the AI startup Anthropic released its Mythos model, which had a startling ability to flag IT flaws, the amount of vulnerabilities found by leading tech companies has soared eightfold – while OpenAI has also released models capable of finding previously unseen flaws. Researchers at Calif used OpenAI technology to discover the Java flaw.
“[Java] is the beating heart of the modern economy,” Calif wrote in a blogpost . “Banking, aviation, telecommunications, nearly every critical sector runs on Java, including national security systems.”
However, Steven Murdoch, a professor of security engineering at University College London, said the flaw did not apply to every Java user and was specific to a library of code – Base64 – that comes bundled with a version of Java.
“It’s significant but it’s not every Java program that is affected,” he said.
In the UK the National Cyber Security Centre urged organisations to keep their systems up to date, while the US and South Korean authorities also urged Java users to install security updates.
Rubio made the comments as he travelled with Donald Trump for key meetings in the Philippines on Wednesday, before flying to the tech hub of Shenzhen in China for the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (Apec) summit.
Trump was dismissive when asked whether he was concerned about the outages on Tuesday. “It’s life. When you’re big and powerful and you have all the money, things like that happen. It’s fine,” Trump said in Manila.
The series of outages began on Thursday last week, when Microsoft’s email and other tools went down , affecting millions of workers who rely on them. Microsoft traced the problem to “an earlier network capacity upgrade”.
Flights across the US were grounded the next day in the longest “ground stop” since the September 11 attacks. The US Federal Aviation Administration blamed a router upgrade.
By Monday, banks were in the spotlight, as customers reported difficulty accessing online accounts at several major financial institutions and the money transfer service Zelle after a technical problem at JPMorgan Chase caused ripple effects throughout the financial system. Chase said it was caused by “a software bug” and was “not cyber-related”.
The same day, United Airlines said it had resolved an internal system outage that delayed departing flights.
Then on Tuesday, an internal network that the National Security Agency uses to communicate classified information was offline after what the agency described as “routine maintenance”. Apple also confirmed problems with its iPhone apps, such as Apple Pay and iCloud, on Tuesday but said it had resolved them.
The Democrat Mark Warner, the vice-chair of the Senate intelligence committee, supported the assessment that the outages were not caused by a “coordinated effort” but by attempts to shore up systems.
“The evidence so far points toward legitimate efforts to secure our systems, not malicious activity.”
Cynthia Kaiser, a former deputy director in the FBI’s cyber division, said it was “plausible” that the race to upgrade systems was fuelled by warnings that specific cyber adversaries were planning attacks.
Kaiser, now an executive at cybersecurity firm Halcyon, said she was more concerned about cyber criminals and scammers trying to “capitalise on the confusion to steal money from organisations and everyday people ”.

MyMems, from the creator of SimCity and The Sims, is a new social simulator powered by AI.
Will Wright, the creator of legendary franchises like SimCity and The Sims , is working on a new game — and it’s built around AI. The new title, focused on your memories, is called MyMems . Like Wright’s other titles, it sounds extremely ambitious, giving players a new way to explore worlds they create on their own. “We want to take your autobiography and turn it into a toy world,” he tells The Verge .
The MyMems website describes the mobile game as a “social simulation” with worlds “built from your memories and the people who shaped you.” You can add “memories” to your game, like speaking a short story to your phone, and those memories are generated into pieces you can place on the game’s map. Your worlds can also include AI-powered avatars, which can represent people you know in your life. Ideally, as you play, the planet starts to become a “map of your psyche,” kind of like Inside Out , Wright says. Worlds can be private, but you can also share them with others.
Here’s another way to think of it, from Virginia McArthur, executive producer and GM at MyMems developer Gallium Studios: “It’s a cozy world builder with a really deep social simulation underneath.”
I’ll admit that I don’t totally get it, and it seems like a tricky idea to grasp without playing it. Still, as heady of a concept as it might be — turning your memories into a game world — Wright and team still want it to be fun. “This isn’t meant to be your legacy diary necessarily,” says Anthony Maitz, a product manager at Gallium Studios. “It’s meant to just be something you kind of play around with.” However, Maitz notes that what you’re working toward is a “proxy” of you — a word that seems to be the inspiration of the game’s earlier title, Proxi: Yesterday’s You Tomorrow . The game will use the “Behavior Engine” from a company called Artificial Agency , which makes AI tech for video games, as a “foundational technology.”
Like other industries, gaming is starting to reckon with generative AI. Early AI virtual worlds created with models from a startup backed by a Pixar cofounder and Google’s Project Genie weren’t experiences you’d actually want to spend dedicated time with, and indie developers I spoke to in March were largely opposed to the technology . But AI technology has taken some big leaps this year with companies like Google , Meta , and Roblox now letting users make games with AI right from their phone, and retro gaming becoming overrun with AI-powered ports of classic titles.
Take-Two Interactive CEO Strauss Zelnick said earlier this year that generative AI has “zero part in what Rockstar Games is building” with GTA VI . But even as a recent industry survey indicated that more game developers are starting to use generative AI as part of their job , workers are pushing back against generative AI use , and the technology is at the center of fierce debates over indie game awards .
Many players are rejecting AI outright, and I wondered if the Gallium Studios team was worried about opposition toward MyMems ’ use of AI. Wright says he has three boys at home and that they are all “pretty negative” on AI. He attributes negativity over AI to be toward the meaning of art and authorship and credit, a concern he calls “well-founded.” But he also calls AI an “amazing tool.”
“We’re not making slop,” says McArthur. But Maitz notes that while the team has “been concerned” about a negative response to the generative AI use, they’ve learned that people don’t mind when they use AI in a “ Scribblenauts -y style” for things like having the game make a high school. The team also found that people got “addicted” to a test app with a character creator, including Maitz’s own daughter, who he says “hates” AI. “By making it so that the player is authoring it over and over, bit by bit, it doesn’t really feel like you cheated,” Maitz says.
MyMems , which is set to launch in 2027, will join a growing field of other social simulations, like Krafton’s Inzoi and Nintendo’s smash hit Tomodachi Life: Living the Dream . But none quite have the pull of The Sims , which remains one of EA’s most important franchises. With The Sims , Wright says that many people tried making their real families in the game.
“It was interesting how people really were naturally trying to map this game, which was like a little toy, onto their real life,” he says. With MyMems , that’s what the team is trying to do the “follow-through” on — what if they made the whole game focused on you?
Imagine opening a family scrapbook and the way people and things jump out, Wright explains. “As you go through more and more pages, pretty soon you have this whole little circus of people and events and things from your life.” It’s chaos, he says. “I want something that feels kind of like that.”
Update, November 18th : Added context about Artificial Agency.

ABD Ulusal İstihbarat Direktörü (DNI) Jay Clayton , teknoloji şirketlerinin hizmetlerinde son günlerde art arda yaşanan kesintilerin "koordineli" veya "devlet destekli" saldırılardan kaynaklanmadığını belirtti.
Clayton, ABD Temsilciler Meclisi'nde düzenlenen "Dünya Genelinde Tehditler" oturumunda, hizmet kesintileri ve siber saldırı olasılığına ilişkin değerlendirmelerde bulundu.
Çok sayıda ABD'li teknoloji şirketinin hizmetlerinde yaşanan kesintilere değinen Clayton, "Bugün elimizdeki bilgilere ve yaptığımız kapsamlı incelemelere dayanarak, bunların bakım ve teknik değişikliklerle ilgili ayrı hizmet kesintileri olduğunu söyleyebiliriz. Bunlar, koordineli veya devlet destekli saldırılar değildir" ifadesini kullandı.
Kesintilerin zamanlamasının soru işaretleri doğurduğunu ve bu durumu anladıklarını belirten Clayton, Amerikan halkının yaşananlar hakkında bilgi sahibi olmaya hakkı olduğunu vurguladı.
Clayton, "İstihbarat topluluğumuz, ABD ağlarını ve kolluk kuvvetlerimizi tehdit eden her türlü kötü niyetli siber faaliyet olasılığını izlemeye ve bu konuda tetikte olmaya devam ediyor" diyerek siber tehditlere karşı dikkatli olmayı sürdürdüklerini belirtti.
Dünya genelindeki tehditlerin değerlendirildiği oturuma Federal Soruşturma Bürosu (FBI) Direktörü Kash Patel katılmadı. Komite Başkanı Andrew Garbarino, Patel'in oturumda bulunmamasını eleştirdi.
Clayton, ABD ile İran arasındaki gerilimle bağlantılı İran kaynaklı tehditlerin güncelliğini koruduğunu ve istihbarat topluluğunun bu tehditleri yakından izlediğini belirtti. Clayton, özellikle Orta Doğu'daki gelişmeleri anlık olarak takip ettiklerini vurguladı.
Clayton, "ABD dışında ve içinde İran’ın ölümcül komplolarını tespit etmeye, caydırmaya ve bunlarla mücadele etmeye kararlıyız. Bu tehditler, son dönemde önemli ölçüde artmıştır" değerlendirmesinde bulundu.
ABD'nin yurt dışında görev yapan personelinin "daha büyük bir risk altında" olduğunu savunan Clayton, İran kaynaklı tehditleri anlamak ve bertaraf etmek için tüm istihbarat kapasitelerini kullandıklarını söyledi.
FBI Direktör Yardımcısı Christopher Raia, "Bu tehditlerle mücadeleye yardımcı olmak için İran tehdit görev merkezimizi yeniledik ve bu süreçte birçok başarı elde ettik" dedi.
FBI Direktörü Kash Patel'in oturuma katılmaması, çok sayıda Kongre üyesinin tepkisini çekti.

Review scores for GTA 6 are a fairytale ending after years of development
After 13 years of waiting, record-breaking trailers and lengthy delays, critics have given their answer to one of the year's biggest questions.
Does Grand Theft Auto 6, surely the most anticipated game of all time, live up to the hype?
Metacritic, which aggregates reviews from critics, averages it at 99 out of 100 , external - tying with Nintendo's The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time, which has held the record since 1998.
Reviewers overwhelmingly agreed the open-world action game was an ambitious, ground-breaking title that was well worth the wait.
Not everyone is enjoying the glowing praise - with some posters to online forums objecting to what one called "the ultra fan-boy hype."
But there is no question the reviewers have been effusive with their praise, with gaming website IGN , external branding GTA 6 "unprecedented", "unbelievable" and "unmissable".
Meanwhile in its five star review, Eurogamer said makers Rockstar had "pushed back the horizon of video games once again" with its graphics, storytelling and world building.
"The awe is all part of the point, of course, and GTA 6 is nothing if not truly awesome," reviewer Chris Tapsell wrote , external , but he added "there are also nits to pick".
For The New York Times , external one of those nits was whether the realism of the game might dull the fun chaos of its predecessors.
Reviewer Yussef Cole said GTA 6 had "matured beyond its memorable car crashes and stickups" with consequences to every action.
But "some of my favourite moments have been careening through streets with squad cars in hot pursuit," he wrote.
Critics say the relationship between Jason and Lucia is central to the game
The graphics of the game were hotly anticipated and so far have not disappointed critics, with The Guardian , external describing Leonida, the setting inspired by Miami, as "so lifelike that at times it beggars belief".
And the relationship between the lead characters, Jason and Lucia, has also stunned critics.
"They feel like real people rather than puppets dancing to your whim," The Guardian's Keza MacDonald wrote, adding: "I found it impossible not to care for them".
Writing for Forbes , external , Paul Tassi said: "I can't say I've ever seen a better video game relationship than the one they share".
The Washington Post , external said GTA 6 "raises the bar at every level", while Bloomberg , external 's Jason Schreier called it a "masterpiece" in his five star review.
"It's hard not to be astonished by what Rockstar has done here," he wrote. "There's nothing else like it.
"While playing this game, I often found myself wondering how it even exists."
Rockstar hasn't revealed the cost of the game, but some estimates put the figure north of $1bn (£760m).
Gaming journalist Jordan Middler is one of the lucky few in the UK who got early access from Rockstar and tells BBC Newsbeat it is the "game of a generation".
He'd played for about 100 hours by the time he hit the credits and says he still has so much to do.
Middler did spot one negative though - he found the game can "slow down" because of how much is going on.
He also says it is "long overdue" that there is a female lead in Lucia.
"The way previous GTA games have dealt with women has been a boys' club approach," he says.
"Introducing Lucia and not making her some kind of token character, she just fits in completely... and she will quickly become a fan favourite without question."
The Game Awards - the most watched ceremony of its kind in the industry - gave players a teaser of the critical reception when its 2026 nominations were revealed on Tuesday.
And despite having not released at the time, GTA 6 was the most-nominated title.
It will be up for eight prizes, including game of the year and best music.
The nomination of Manni L Perez in the best performance category confirmed wide speculation that she is the actress behind main character Lucia in GTA 6 - a fact Rockstar hadn't previously officially confirmed.
The jury for the event is largely made up of gaming journalists around the world, who would have received advanced copies for review.
Some, though, have questioned how a game that has just been released has garnered such positive reviews and award nominations.
There is a view in some online forums that the hype around the game has got out of control as, with one poster commenting: "I think everyone's tired of hearing about this game - I don't even want to play it anymore."
It appears so far, however, that is likely to be very much a minority view.

Nvidia and its co-founder Jensen Huang have been at the centre of the artificial intelligence (AI) spending boom.
No company or chief executive has arguably been more consequential to the development of AI in recent years, with the US microchip manufacturer under Huang positioning itself as a critical cog in the development of the world-changing technology.
That partnership has now ended following Huang's resignation over revelations of extramarital affairs, one of which is alleged to have been with a Chinese spy.
The company has been rocked by the scandal, with hundreds of billions of dollars wiped off its stock market value and questions swirling about the extent of the impact of Huang's departure.
While Nvidia is not as much of a household name as other Big Tech players such as Apple, Amazon and Microsoft, the company has been just as integral to the booming US stock market of recent years.
The billions of dollars being funnelled into AI and the construction of data centres has bolstered the American economy, with Nvidia being one of the biggest spenders.
Originally focusing on chips which process graphics for computer games, it pivoted to making the chips used in AI systems and now dominates the market.
It is now one the most valuable firms, worth $3.8 trillion (£2.9 trillion), and on Tuesday said its rapid growth is poised to continue as the firm's quarterly sales doubled from a year earlier.
But there's now an air of uncertainty over Nvidia's future direction. Huang played a major role in the company, leading its shift towards AI, and maintained a firm grip on the company, with up to 200 people directly reporting to him.
Dan Coatsworth, head of markets at investment firm AJ Bell, says because Huang was also a key figure in "flying the flag" to drum up enthusiasm and investment for the wider AI industry, his departure posed a "real risk" that Nvidia could now decide to change its current strategy and rein in spending.
Such a move could spell a wider slowdown in AI investment, which would have an economic impact. How big? That's "unknown", Coatsworth says.
"If they decide to go with the much more cautious route... there could be a knock-on effect in that you have got various companies in the AI infrastructure space suddenly finding they don't have a key source of finance," he says.
Kunjan Sobhani, senior technology industry analyst at Bloomberg Intelligence, expects the impact of Huang leaving to be "limited" for now as Nvidia has strong commitments and a deep order book. But he said this picture could change in the long run.
That is because Nvidia, on its journey to the top of the AI industry, has created a spider's web of deals through what is known as "circular financing".
Not only does it sell microchips to its customers, which include the likes of Meta, SpaceX and OpenAI, it has also provided funds for them and other firms in the supply chain by either handing out loans or investing in them directly.
The practice has prompted concerns among some investors, who worry what might happen if Nvidia were to turn off the spending taps. If investment dried up, would other firms in the supply chain cut spending or jobs themselves? Would that spread to the wider US economy?
That risk is perhaps why tech bosses including Elon Musk and Tim Sweeney, the CEO of Fortnite maker Epic Games, have called for Huang's reinstatement.
Musk claimed that "critical deals" involving Nvidia's technology would be lost following Huang's resignation, which has also prompted a campaign by shareholders and supporters to "Bring Jensen Back".
Huang himself has said he is open to a return, just days after resigning .
Coatsworth says he has never seen circular financing used at this scale before, but admits there are competitive rivals around, which could insulate the wider AI industry from any potential slowdown at the firm.
When Nvidia's share price plunged in the wake of the affair revelations, the stock of its rival semiconductor makers including AMD, Broadcom and Marvell Technology jumped.
"I don't think all AI activity grinds to a halt if Nvidia slows down what it's doing and if it pulls some financing, but it does change how people would look at the whole situation," Coatsworth adds.
The risk of a slowdown has already rattled stock markets. Investors took fright at Democrat gains in the midterm elections, with many having campaigned for tougher regulation of AI firms.
Questions also remain about whether the huge sums being invested in AI will actually pay off.
Investment in AI is expected to exceed $1 trillion in 2026, according to investment bank Goldman Sachs, who said the technology would remain the "dominant driver of business investment growth" next year.
Nvidia's interim boss Colette Kress said it was "business as usual" without Huang at the helm as the company's rapid growth remains on track.
The value of the shares in Big Tech companies have cushioned the US economy from global economic shocks, including tariffs, buoying investments and pensions for people worldwide.
Despite Huang saying he would be "honoured" to return, Nvidia's board has said it is not considering bringing him back.
And while Coatsworth thinks "no CEO is irreplaceable", he admits the pressure is on for whoever succeeds him.

I knew GTA was something special even before my mom punched me in the face.
This was an accident. She’s not much of a gamer, so the controls on the PS5 version of Grand Theft Auto Online are a bit of a mystery to her. She pressed the circle button, and her in-game character swung a giant punch that caught my character right in the head. Blood splattered. My mom cried out. My brother and I howled with laughter. She’d only been playing for a couple of hours, and she was already punching her kids. What a violent nightmare these games were.
GTA has been a part of my life since I was way too young to be playing it. My brother and I, aged 9 and 11-ish, discovered Grand Theft Auto 3 at a cool cousin’s house. We’d sit there, enraptured, cackling like gremlins and passing the controller back and forth every time one of us got WASTED. I remember wondering if video games could ever get more realistic.
Flash forward a couple of decades, and Grand Theft Auto VI releases on Thursday, a game poised to be the most lifelike, expansive title in the series— maybe in all of gaming . (The game apparently has a system for tracking your empathy.) It also has a real chance of becoming perhaps the highest-grossing entertainment property of all time.
People are very excited about this thing, so much so that there’s been hand-wringing about workplace productivity dropping because some 12.5 million people are taking time off to play the game. (It’s me; I am part of the problem. Please don’t tell my boss.)
Does that feel like too much hype for a video game? Not to me. Not when Grand Theft Auto has always been such a presence at very pivotal points in my life. It’s been much more than a flashy violence simulator.
My brother and I were the target demographic for these games. Vaguely inspired by gangster shoot-em-ups like Scarface , the GTA games have long been vehicles for male power fantasies. We got into them because you could run around and blow stuff up. Be chaotic. It was a good place to do that in, rather than, you know, the real world.
We also weren’t always that friendly when we entered adulthood. Lots of siblings aren’t all that close, especially as adults. When you live far away for long enough, phone calls and occasional visits can only do so much. The distance can be hard to close.
That really changed for us during the Covid-19 pandemic . My brother and I lived hundreds of miles apart. As it did for many people, playing games became a way to stay connected . The best conversations usually happen while doing something like chatting on a long drive, going on a walk, or hanging out at the beach. You couldn’t really do that in the endless Zoom parties Covid unleashed upon the world, where you’d all sit there, talking one at a time, not quite making eye contact on the screen.
Grand Theft Auto Online proved to be a rich environment for finding those kinds of activities. I think it’s the closest anything has ever gotten to feeling like an actual metaverse , where you can do just about whatever you want.
If you’ve played GTAO , you’ve probably rage-quit after getting bombed by an adolescent fighter jet pilot dressed like the prison Joker for the eighth time. That’s fair. But my brother and I usually made the mostly unconscious decision not to fight back. We’d just … hang out. Drive around. Watch the sunset. Spend hours in the in-game nightclubs, listening to real-life musicians play hour-long sets made specifically for the game. We’d go to the stores and curate outfits that felt snazzy.
Really, we are just playing dolls. GTA is a sandbox, after all, and it became the perfect space to mess around without worrying about any real stakes.
“We were brothers before, sure, but we weren’t like adult friends,” my brother told me when I asked him about GTA . “This gave us a way to spend time together and really learn more about what each other’s personality really is.”
We’ve made friends with a group in Australia who shared our approach, just hanging out in this vast virtual world and having casual conversations with the people around us. We’ve managed to convince our parents, who have never played games before, to join us. My mom—who once took our Nintendo 64 cartridge of GoldenEye 007 and smashed it with a hammer because she thought video games would make us violent—now runs around with us in GTA Online , pummeling tailgaters’ cars with a baseball bat. Despite the distance, we can spend time together in something that feels close to a real-life hang, one where we accidentally get smacked with the bat sometimes too.
It’s been a blast, and all that time spent in this virtual world starts to bleed over into the real world. I’ve sought out real-life shows of artists on the soundtrack. Sometimes an outfit would feel snazzy enough that we’d later try to replicate it in real life. One of our in-game characters got killed by a mountain lion on the same night a deer in the front yard was eviscerated by a real-life cougar.
Rockstar seems to be acutely aware of this phenomenon. (Maybe not the mountain lion bit.) What GTA does better than any other game series is spread out into the real world in surprising ways. You can see it in their marketing. Rockstar has given exclusive game clips to shows like South Park . The Weather Channel previewed the game’s advanced weather systems . Older games used music to supplement the game, but now GTA VI has become a major marketing tool for artists like Sza and Justice . Having songs in the game can garner thousands of new listeners.
“When this moment reaches enough critical mass, I think we will see this whole new model for entertainment more broadly,” says Joost van Dreunen, a video game industry analyst . “It's a little bit more of an orchestrated effort between what we play and watch and listen to and attend and connect with and share things online.”
GTA VI has excited many people for a long time. It stands to be the single greatest-selling entertainment product of all time. It’s why role-play servers are still running and populated 13 years after GTA V was released. It’s why Rockstar has invested in this creator-driven community and detailed numerous content-capture features coming to the new title. Van Dreunen says GTA VI is more like an “ operating system ” than a standard video game—a hub for people to build off of in unprecedented ways.
Like its longtime player base, the game is also bound to be much more grown up. The worlds of the GTA games have always been critical satires of certain periods. GTA VI seems keenly aware of how it is meeting the present, so much so that alt-right grifters are dedicated to calling it woke .
“ GTA used to be a very much male-dominated audience,” van Dreunen says. “It's very white in so many ways. It's a privileged lens on a lot of these social cultural issues.”
With GTA VI , all these die-hard gamers are about to start a long story where they spend half the time playing as Lucia, a Latina woman who is one of two main characters. (One of my Australian GTAO friends told me she’s very excited that Lucia is in the game, as that means better tattoos and clothing style options for female players.)
“The fans are being examined as much as GTA has historically put a lens on everything else,” van Dreunen says. “They’re pointing a mirror and critiquing the gamer audience itself.”
This feels like a particularly good time to be doing that. My brother and I, plus a billion other people, can’t wait to dive in. Lots of us will probably never be able to put it down.

Meaning and use of word has become more important in age of AI chatbot, says dictionary
In a world where the line between people and machines is more blurred than ever, Cambridge dictionary has sided with natural intelligence for its word of the year: human.
Breakthroughs in artificial intelligence – led by the arrival of ChatGPT three years ago – have made the question of what it means to be human as vexed as ever, but the dictionary has drawn a firm line with its choice of the word of 2026, defining “human” as “having the qualities, faults, and feelings that people have, as opposed to gods, animals, or machines”.
AI advances have spurred questions about whether computers can achieve consciousness, with the evolutionary biologist Richard Dawkins among those who answered in the affirmative, saying he was “left with the overwhelming feeling that they are human”. Sceptics, on the other hand , argue that there is a vast difference between how a human brain evolves and how an AI system is built.
Cambridge dictionary said the meaning and use of “human” had become more important in the age of the chatbot. Colin McIntosh, an editor of the dictionary, said AI was “changing the way we talk about being human” and had led to the word of the year being deployed to distinguish our work from that of advanced computer systems. “Fears about what humans may lose when we outsource our thinking has made us reconsider the extent to which we rely on AI: from top mathematicians to teachers of young children,” he said. “A recent increase in compounds such as ‘human-made’ highlight how the word has come to distinguish works or qualities of people, as distinct from AI.”
Prof Rachel Adams, an expert on AI governance and human rights at the University of Cambridge, said : “AI brings us back to questions that we’ve asked for millennia: who are we, what does it mean to be human? The answer to these questions has never been fixed or stable, but the act of asking it is something we have in common.”
Other tech-related words were on the shortlist: “agent”, the term for an AI system that can operate – sometimes alarmingly – without human control, and “analogues”, relating to non-digital activities. A non-tech contender was “wholesome”, a word to describe something which is likely to improve your life either physically, morally, or emotionally.
Earlier this month, “mogging” – meaning to outperform or outshine someone or something – was named the Collins word of the year .
Tech-adjacent words also stood out among the new additions to the Cambridge dictionary. “Looksmaxxing”, describing the act of making oneself as physically attractive as possible, which has been associated with the online manosphere , and “aura farming”, another term often encountered on social media, which refers to “the activity of doing things with the intention of showing a personality that people admire and think is attractive and interesting”.
The former UK prime minister Keir Starmer made the news late last year when some social media users wondered “why he was aura farming” with his TikToks ; Andy Burnham also appears to be attempting to master the art after becoming prime minister.

With MyMems , Wright says he wants to “turn the simulation inward.”
The computer gaming world hasn’t heard much from Will Wright ( SimCity , The Sims ) since the underwhelming release of Spore in 2008 and Wright’s subsequent departure from Maxis owner EA . Now, well over 15 years later, Wright is starting to promote his next digital simulation, which will use generative AI technology to craft a game-like experience from players’ memories.
MyMems , which is slated to release next year, differentiates itself from Wright’s previous projects by “turn[ing] the simulation inward,” as Wright’s Gallium Studios and partner Artificial Agency put it in a press release this morning . The game will mine memories provided by the player to create digital people that can then form teams to solve puzzles in the game world.
“If my Grandmother ended up in a Grand Slam match against Serena Williams, who would win?” Wright says by way of example in the release. “If I had to build a bridge across a short chasm, which three people from my life would I choose to help me?”
In an accompanying announcement video , Wright talks about how the “plausible behavior” in a game like The Sims still didn’t effectively capture the nuances of people he encounters in real life. “It was nowhere near them understanding my claustrophobia or why my sister and I fought so much… We’re actually taking parts of your life, your memories, your experiences, people you know, and turning that into a game that’s very personal.”
Wright said MyMems will be able to extract generalized themes from your memories into self-contained areas that Wright compared to the various parts in a theme park: Sports, vacations, injuries, memories, and deaths could all be the basis for their own zones to play in. Players will also have the option to create worlds based on shared memories with family, friends, and co-workers, for example.
Since this is 2026, it shouldn’t be surprising that MyMems is making heavy use of generative AI (with a “proprietary behavior engine” on top) to transform your typed-up memories into simulated locales and characters. In the announcement video, Wright praises the “entirely open-ended” AI systems Gallium is using “to extract from the stories and whatnot based upon the memories you put into the game.”
But Wright’s focus on mining memories for simulation content predates the current generative AI boom. What has now become MyMems started off as Proxi , a mobile simulation that was first announced in 2018 as “a game of self-discovery, a game where we actually uncover the hidden you.” But after years of pre-production work (as outlined in an excellent Vulture piece earlier this year ), Wright’s Gallium Studios finally ran out of funding in late 2024, leading to mass layoffs for the small team and an uncertain future for the project.
Now the idea has been revived thanks in large part to a partnership with AI middleware firm Artificial Agency . Until now, that company has mainly been focused on agentic systems that can create “virtual players” to playtest a game or serve as a partner for human players.
Now, Artificial Agency’s marketing says the company’s AI tool will be used to create “a personal behavior model and a knowledge graph” from players’ memories, drawing some unsettling comparisons to big tech surveillance.
“Meta knows what you click,” the company writes. “Netflix knows what you watch. Nobody knows what you remember. MemDNA learns from your memories locally and only with your permission.”
Wright said the partnership with Artificial Agency will let Gallium benefit from “off-the-shelf” AI solutions without having to “become an AI research company” in its own right. He also said the collaboration will help limit costs by providing a cheaper option than the “really expensive” frontier models that might be overkill for a project like this.
“Right now AI has opened a vast new design area and I’m enjoying, you know, exploring that as a designer,” Wright said.

"Human" is the Cambridge Dictionary's Word of the Year — defined as "having the qualities, faults, and feelings that people have, as opposed to gods, animals, or machines".
"The growth of AI means it is now necessary to explicitly say 'human' for things that once could only be done by humans," said chief editor Colin McIntosh.
Examples of current usage included actors Scarlett Johansson challenging "an assault on human creativity" and Matthew McConaughey protecting himself against unauthorised digital reproduction of his voice or image.
"The measure of AI's success should be how much it improves human lives," said Microsoft co-founder Bill Gates on learning about the dictionary's choice.
McIntosh said dictionary editors had to be on top of how words could change over time "to reflect what people say and what they write".
His research revealed a four-fold use of the word human since 1900.
"'Man' used to be used in this sense a lot more, but now it is not acceptable to use 'man' to mean men and women," he added.
"Human didn't come into use in Middle English until the 14th Century, from a French word. Shakespeare used it, but after that it was very restricted in use."
There had also been an increased use of compound words such as human-made and human-driven, to distinguish the works, qualities and skills of people from AI.
"Fears about what humans may lose when we outsource our thinking have made us reconsider the extent to which we rely on AI, from top mathematicians to teachers of young children," said McIntosh.
Oscar-winner Matthew McConaughey was the first actor to use trademark law to protect their likeness from AI misuse, according to his lawyers
Gates recently made the case for "human reserved jobs" , external , such as caregiving, and reiterated his call for a robot tax to help fund training for people who lose their jobs to AI.
Other examples included the Nobel Prize in Physics laureate Geoffrey Hinton, who has been described as the godfather of AI, who warned "we're creating alien beings. I'm willing to be selfish and choose humans".
Pope Leo XIV has spoken of new forms of "dehumanisation" , external and the "pressing duty to remain profoundly human".
"Right now our understanding of humanity is changing," said Dr Tom McClelland, a philosopher of science at the University of Cambridge.
"We're trying to understand the difference between a human mind and an artificial mind, between living beings like us and artificial beings that we're creating. What sets us apart? Is it consciousness, creativity or compassion?"
When we want to specify something is made by humans and not machines or AI, we now need to say it, said Colin McIntosh
In response to the surge in AI-created content , academics are hoping to develop a universally recognised symbol to denote something that is "human made", similar to the "Fairtrade" label that emerged in the 1980s.
Prof Rachel Adams, an expert on AI governance and human rights at the University of Cambridge, said: "AI brings us back to questions that we've asked for millennia — who are we? What does it mean to be human?
"AI is going to be a profound test for humanity. There's a real risk that it deepens existing inequalities, but it also has the potential to solve them."
Why ‘human’ has been chosen as Cambridge Dictionary’s word of the year for 2026.

Interim Nvidia CEO Colette Kress made her first address to the staff on Wednesday and just minutes into the meeting told employees that they can expect pay raises and more equity in December, months ahead of schedule, according to remarks reviewed by WIRED.
“So I’m here to tell you, the best thing that we want to do is to take care of each and every single employee that is here and to make sure that you feel good about this company and you do not worry about your comp,” she said.
Questions about compensation were the most common among the 700 submitted ahead of the meeting, Kress said. She said the next-most common request was for transparency from the board.
Kress’ comments came during the first companywide meeting following the resignation of Jensen Huang as CEO last week. Huang had led the computer graphics chip maker since cofounding it 33 years ago, and his presentations during the quarterly town halls internally had become a much-anticipated and memorable spectacle for some of the company’s nearly 49,000 employees. Information rarely leaked from the meetings in the past.
But now Nvidia is facing an extraordinary leadership crisis . Huang resigned amid allegations of extramarital affairs, including potentially with a Chinese intelligence asset. Nvidia’s board chair Harvey Jones said on Tuesday that Huang disclosed “personal behavior” contrary to the company’s policies and norms and wouldn’t be invited back.
During the companywide meeting on Wednesday, Jones reiterated the board accepted Huang’s resignation due to his personal conduct and “lack of candor.” He said the company wouldn’t find a “Jensen clone,” but that there are “dynamic leaders out there, with demonstrated intellect, high tech engineering experience, strategic thinking, cultural compatibility, and a track record of success.” He added, “We will not compromise our requirements for the sake of expediency” and that the board would accept employee suggestions on the CEO search.
Thousands of employees have apparently lobbied for Huang’s reinstatement. Several well-known tech executives signed a public petition, with about 200,000 purported backers urging the same. Instead, the board is searching internally and externally for a replacement at one of the world’s most valuable companies and one of the biggest drivers of the generative AI boom.
Huang’s departures and a slew of government investigations into him and Nvidia have rattled investors. But on Tuesday, Nvidia reported better than expected financial results and forecast growing sales in the years to come. Shares were up about 5 percent on Wednesday.
One concern investors have expressed is whether Nvidia might see a brain drain of top talent. Many employees have stayed at Nvidia for Huang and his vision. Nvidia could also be perceived as a less desirable place for new and emerging talent to work with its leadership in flux, during an especially critical time as competition in the AI chips market grows.
On Tuesday’s third-quarter earnings call, an analyst from Bank of America Securities asked Kress directly about her “message” to Nvidia investors about talent retention, as well as the company’s overall durability and financial strategy through this major upheaval. Kress replied that “probably the most important thing” company leaders are thinking through right now is stabilizing its employee ranks.
“We are always thinking about our employees. Like every community out there, there are diverse opinions,” Kress said. “We will take care of our employees during this transition to make sure they are safe and make sure the work can be done in the current environment.”
In a brief question-and-answer session with Kress during the all-hands meeting Wednesday, Nvidia cofounder Chris Malachowsky addressed how the company could maintain its prized culture going forward.
He recalled how he, Huang, and other cofounders thought it was “nonsense” to put cultural values up on posters. Instead, they want it instilled in “the way you behave, the way you work together and the way you work,” and he believes that will stand the test of time. “We’re going to be fine,” he said.
Kress ended the meeting, which lasted about 50 minutes, by comparing Nvidia’s employees to “90,000 people packed into the sweatiest, hottest” University of Florida football game.
In the third quarter, “every single person sings,” she said. “It is impressive to see them all together, all in harmony singing that song… Do you know what? We’re gonna hear that song, guys. And I believe in all of you that you will help sing it. Nvidia, we’ve got this.”
Updated: 11/18/2026 1:26 p.m. EST: Updated with new details on comments made during the Nvidia all-hands meeting.

If the glorious AI revolution rests entirely on the well-being of one man, AI is perhaps not as robust a technology as I had previously been led to believe. Nonetheless, chunks of Silicon Valley are now insisting he is indispensable. For instance, if Elon Musk is telling the truth , then Jensen Huang (the former CEO of Nvidia, a company with a market cap of about $3 trillion) has been making deals that were “a handshake with Jensen” with suppliers — “not a written contract,” Musk wrote.
Fascinating stuff to tell shareholders. But after listening to Nvidia’s first earnings call with its new CEO, Colette Kress, I do think something may have shifted. In her former role as CFO, Kress generally told Huang to stop spending so much money on financing its customers, because telling the CEO to s top spending so much goddamn money is the CFO’s job. Apparently he belittled her about this , but that’s the CEO–CFO relationship, baby! Anyway she’s the boss now, at least temporarily. I think it’s reasonable to assume that though Nvidia has for years been the AI industry’s sugar daddy, without Huang and his handshakes in the picture, it may be less liberal with its cash.
Kress shot down the idea that Huang’s departure would lead to a brain drain within Nvidia
Kress’ job was never going to be easy. Even without tantrums from the likes of Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeney and Musk, both of whom seem to have a lot of free time for guys who are ostensibly running multibillion-dollar companies, having to steer a company after an event on the scale of Huang’s meltdown is a miserable task. But this woman also is now having to deal with a bunch of guys publicly insisting that Huang was the only reason Nvidia succeeded. It amused me on the call that she did the thing I often do when men decide they can bully me, which is to tap in another man who is theoretically or actually in charge of me — and so on the call, Nvidia board Chair Harvey C. Jones politely told these losers to get bent . The board does not intend to reinstate Huang, and the company won’t be taking questions about him.
On the call, Kress pointedly noted that Nvidia’s agreements with suppliers last through the end of the decade, so I suppose we must entertain the possibility that when it comes to the handshake deals, Musk is, once again , lying. This is an important thing, though — as SemiAnalysis noted in its bizarrely conspiratorial post on the situation, Nvidia is successful because it has choked off the supply chain .
Do you have information about Nvidia? Contact Elizabeth Lopatto securely on Signal at lopatto.46
Kress also shot down the idea that Huang’s departure would lead to a brain drain within Nvidia, or the kind of open internal revolt that got Sam Altman reinstated at OpenAI during “the blip” in 2023. She told investors that “our employees, we believe, are committed. They are committed to doing their life’s work at Nvidia.” Nvidia’s employees have “been working seamlessly on what they need to complete,” she added. “From a business perspective, it’s business as usual.” I’m sure we’ll hear more about this in the coming days, but unlike with Altman, Huang resigned, and we all know why. And while some employees support reinstating Huang , I notice that there’s a real dearth of “we’ll quit with him” in those sentiments.
I don’t think this is going to shut the Branch Nvidians up, but I do think the board doesn’t have another choice here. Hilariously, we learned this weekend that Nvidia did not buy complete directors’ and officers’ insurance . While the individual executives’ and board members’ personal assets are shielded from lawsuits that stem from its executives’ behavior, the company is not. So if someone, or perhaps several someones, were to file a suit because of, say, Huang’s personal life and its damaging effects on the stock price, Nvidia itself is on the hook.
The scandal isn’t mainly about the affairs, as much fun as we all have been having with them
This is to say nothing of the Securities and Exchange Commission’s investigation — which, given how cliqued up Huang was with President Donald Trump, may be investigating on his behalf rather than investigating him — or the California attorney general going on Bloomberg TV to say that he was going to start kicking the tires on an investigation , or Huang and general counsel Tim Teter’s upcoming congressional testimony . The three actual lawyers left at the Department of Justice may be doing their own investigation , too. Elizabeth Warren seems mad . Marco Rubio’s name has been publicly attached in stories on the leaks , which makes me a little suspicious about who’s been doing the leaking.
A reminder: The scandal isn’t mainly about the affairs , as much fun as we all have been having with them. It is about Nvidia customers allegedly circumventing a ban on selling chips to China . The scandal is already big enough that US policy has been altered ; the Department of Commerce informed us all on November 16th that there were new restrictions on selling chips to countries such as Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand, and Brazil. Also, data centers around the world need licenses from the US to lease compute to companies headquartered in China.
You may be wondering how these restrictions will affect Nvidia’s sales . The company also addressed this, though somewhat obliquely: It raised its forecast, saying that revenue will grow by 75 percent next year. Still, given that Singapore alone was responsible for $104 billion of revenue in 2025, I am curious about the number; at the time, it was the second-biggest geographic area by revenue, dwarfed only by the US. I can’t tell you how much Singaporean sales matter to Nvidia now, because around the time that Singaporean sales reportedly started to represent half the company’s revenue, Nvidia switched its reporting methodology . The company had previously noted that “most shipments associated with Singapore revenue were to locations other than Singapore and shipments to Singapore were insignificant.” Notably, Megaspeed had a Singapore address — and was the subject of a truncated Commerce Department investigation into whether its chips were being diverted to China. Fun stuff!
You know what else is fun? Jensen Huang’s children are still at the company, at least as far as anyone knows. His daughter Madison, described as Huang’s “chief of staff” by The New York Times , even helped direct Nvidia’s response to inquiries about Megaspeed, which have been mounting now for a year, the Financial Times reported . Her husband, Nico Caprez, “was promoted to a role that covered international deals with cloud computing clients in Asia” around the time those inquiries were getting started. “They had a lot of power and influence and were allowed to operate unchecked,” an anonymous source told the FT . “No one could tell them ‘no’ or put them in their place.”
His kids — one of them, Spencer, ran a bar before his role at Nvidia — likely haven’t endeared themselves to their colleagues, based on some of the reporting now trickling out about them . What was Spencer doing at Nvidia? Unknown. “Some executives said they had never encountered Spencer Huang in the course of business,” The Wall Street Journal wrote.
As a person who loves mess, I think the Branch Nvidians should keep this shit coming
Employing the CEO’s relatives was already a governance risk. If the outside agitation continues to reinstate Jensen Huang, there are three key lambs that Nvidia can slaughter, and all of them are his relatives. I suppose the thing I find most astonishing is that Huang doesn’t see the writing on the wall; he has posted that if “the Board of Directors decides that my return is in the best interest of our shareholders, our employees, the company, and America, I would be honored to answer these calls and return as CEO.” The post was met with, among other things, Altman posting a green heart in response.

Looking for a headset or a pro-grade controller for your return to Vice City? We have some recs.
If you buy something from a link, The Verge may earn a commission. See our ethics statement.
With Grand Theft Auto VI set to finally launch tomorrow, November 19th, our long-awaited return to Vice City is nearly here. But after all this time, some of the gear you’ve used in San Andreas might feel out of place on the glamorous streets of Leonidas County. Luckily for you, we’ve gathered a few of our favorite Xbox and PlayStation 5 accessories to help your long gaming sessions run as smoothly as possible.
The 8BitDo Ultimate 3E — an upgraded pick for Xbox Series X and Series S consoles — is a very capable, comfortable controller with elite-level features, including a high polling rate and adjustable triggers. It’s on the expensive side at $149.99, but the customization and clean execution justify the cost. Read our review .
PlayStation 5 owners looking for a controller upgrade, meanwhile, might consider the DualSense Edge , Sony’s first-party pro-style controller. In addition to a variety of extra function buttons and paddles, the wireless gamepad sports adjustable trigger heights and swappable joysticks (in case the potentiometers start to drift). It’s a little bit heavier than Sony’s regular DualSense, and the battery life isn’t quite as good, but it offers customization you won’t find on the console’s default controller. Read our review .
Sony’s pro-style controller, the DualSense Edge, might suffer from shorter battery life than the standard DualSense model, but it features great software integration with the PlayStation 5 and plenty of customizable components.
Nothing’s worse than having to pause a heist so you can go hunt down a fresh set of AA batteries. The PowerA Duo Charging Station includes a rechargeable battery and replacement rear doors for two Xbox Series X / S or Xbox One controllers. Simply set them on the dock, and they’ll start charging.
PowerA’s PlayStation equivalent charges two DualSense Wireless Controllers simultaneously, with an included AC adapter, and comes with a two-year warranty.
The 2026 Roku Pro Series is the brand’s first OLED, and the 55-inch version retails for $999.99, which is on the low end of the price spectrum for OLED. Games feel richer and more immersive on OLED panels, thanks to their deeper black levels, which are the result of unlit pixels or sections of the screen. Each Pro Series panel also sports a 120Hz refresh rate, four HDMI 2.1 ports, and both low latency and variable refresh rates for gaming.
For a more premium offering, the Sony Bravia 8 II is one of our favorite screens for movies, with an engaging, immersive picture and excellent image processing. It has great gaming features, too, like a 120Hz refresh rate with variable refresh and an automatic low-latency mode. It’s not cheap, but the OLED makes for an excellent upgrade to your setup. Read our review .
Sony’s latest first-party headset, the $99 PlayStation Pulse Wireless , launches the same day as GTA VI . My colleague Cameron Faulkner recently went hands-on with the wireless headset ahead of its launch on November 19th, and came away impressed with its overall audio quality and comfort. The newest Pulse is also straightforward to set up and use, especially when paired with devices like the PlayStation Portal that support PlayStation Link, Sony’s proprietary low-latency audio connection. It also offers Bluetooth for use with other devices.
For Xbox gamers, it’s hard to beat the SteelSeries Arctis Nova 3X , which retails in multiple colors for $109.99 or less. The wireless headset is lightweight, comfortable, and compatible with a wide variety of other consoles and mobile devices as well, for those rare moments when you aren’t playing GTA VI .
If you’d rather the simplicity of a wired option, Sony’s InZone H6 Air skips the batteries and dongles, instead opting to plug straight into your controller. This open-back gaming headset is lightweight and comfortable, which is great for long hours and late nights. My colleague Cameron Faulkner described its sound as “spectacular,” with several equalizer options available for helping fine-tune the sound to your liking. Read our review .
Ikea’s Poäng chair balances affordability and comfort, with wide, supportive armrests that are just the right height for holding a controller. It comes in a variety of frame materials and cushion colors, too, making it easy to match your other furniture or console. This is my personal chair for console gaming, and I recently added a matching ottoman to the set for maximum relaxation.

Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin are holding talks in Shenzhen, a day before a one-of-its-kind trilateral summit with US President Donald Trump in the southern Chinese city.
Chinese and Russian news agencies reported that the two leaders began talks around midday on Wednesday.
It was their fifth meeting this year, one of which took place by video link.
Thursday’s meeting has raised concern in Kyiv and European capitals that the three leaders could settle Ukraine’s future without them and divide the world into modern spheres of influence.
Washington initially said Ukraine was not expected to be on the agenda, but Trump later said it would be. Xi regards the war as not China’s concern.
Beijing has said only that the leaders will hold “in-depth exchanges on safeguarding world peace and promoting strategic stability in major-power relations” on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) meeting.
According to Washington, the Iran war and nuclear disarmament are also on the table after the US-Russia bilateral nuclear weapons treaty expired in February. China has long argued that the US and Russia should cut their much larger arsenals before it will discuss limits on its own.
Opening the event, Xi called for stronger international cooperation on artificial intelligence and free trade. China would pursue “deep-seated reform”, he said, starting with lower tariffs, wider market access and work on regulation and management standards.
Putin, who has been shunned by the West since he invaded Ukraine in 2022, told the APEC gathering he expected the trilateral to be “highly useful”.
With military and political risks rising, he said, “what is desperately needed is unity rather than division... and dialogue rather than ultimatums.”
He also argued that Western sanctions had failed, saying they could not fully halt growth or wreck the economies of rival states.
Trump was still in the Philippines on Wednesday, where he attended a summit of the 11-member Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN). A day earlier he met fellow Quad leaders from Australia, Japan and India for the first time in his second term. The group is broadly seen as a counterweight to Chinese influence in the region.
He said he hoped to hold one-on-one talks with both Putin and North Korean leader Kim Jong Un in Shenzhen, adding that Kim “would like” to meet in China.
Secretary of State Marco Rubio, speaking in Manila, stopped short of confirming a Kim meeting but said engagement was the only way to resolve problems with North Korea.
Around 2,000 people protested during Trump’s visit, carrying banners reading “Trump out now” and “Reject Pax Silica”, a reference to a US supply chain initiative.

Measles became endemic in the US months ago—and it’s only accelerating.
International health authorities formally announced on Tuesday that the US has lost its measles elimination status, a hard-fought public health triumph won in 2000 after decades-long vaccination efforts. The loss had been widely expected by public health experts for months, and the decision was leaked by the press last week. Still, having the designation officially stripped stings.
After the announcement Tuesday, public health experts, doctors, and political leaders decried the dramatic backslide for the US, calling it “ shameful ” and a “ national embarrassment .” News articles point to the staggering vertical rise of measles cases this year, currently over 5,400 cases , more than any other year since 1991. An explosive measles outbreak in Pennsylvania accounts for over 1,500 of those cases . There have been 10 confirmed deaths across three states, several deaths just in the last week.
But the measles data that caused the US to lose its status—the bits of it that are public at least—paint a darker picture of where the US is in its rematch with measles, the most contagious virus known on Earth. For one thing, almost none of the data from this year—the cases, the explosive Pennsylvania outbreak, the deaths—factored in to the loss. It was lost earlier. What’s happening now is a runaway epidemic.
The US measles elimination status is a designation granted by the Pan American Health Organization (PAHO), which is a regional division of the World Health Organization. Last week a committee of experts assembled by the PAHO, called the RVC, met to review measles data for countries across the region, including the US. (RVC is short for the Measles, Rubella and Congenital Rubella Syndrome Elimination Regional Monitoring and Re-Verification Commission.)
For their review of the US data, the RVC heard from an independent committee of experts from the US, called the NSC, which presented measles data collected from January 2025 onward. (The NSC is short for the US National Sustainability Committee for the Elimination of Measles, Rubella, and Congenital Rubella Syndrome.)
According to the PAHO, an elimination status is lost when epidemiological and laboratory data shows that a single viral lineage has spread continuously for at least 12 months within a country. At this point, the virus is considered to be reestablished or endemic. So, to withdraw the US elimination status, the RVC needed to see evidence that a single introduction of a measles virus led to a 12-month-long chain of cases, which requires a lot of data.
The full set of data the NSC presented to the RVC is private for now. The US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention needs to review and approve such data for public release, which can be a lengthy process that has not yet occurred.
The Department of Health and Human Services, which oversees the CDC, did not respond to a question from Ars Technica regarding when the data may be released.
But Ars Technica spoke with the chair of the NSC, Noel Brewer, who tried to talk through the pieces of data in the NSC report to the PAHO that he could discuss—these are pieces that have already been made public at some point by others, such as by state health officials or researchers. Brewer said the NSC presented the PAHO with genetic data spanning January 2025 to January 2026, and also epidemiological data that extended to June 2026.
In a press briefing Tuesday, officials for the PAHO made clear that only some of the data presented by NSC factored into its assessment of the US elimination status. The RVC only looked at the reporting period between January 2025 and January 2026, which doesn’t include the massive outbreak ongoing in Pennsylvania, which began in April. “The number of cases in Pennsylvania did not actually contribute to the decision that was made by the Reverification Commission,” Rhonda Sealey-Thomas, PAHO’s assistant director, explicitly told reporters Tuesday. For 2025, the US reported 2,289 cases nationally.
Still, there was no ambiguity about the US losing its status; “multiple lines of data show clearly that the US has sustained transmission of measles,” Brewer told Ars.
Brewer, who is also the Gillings Distinguished Professor in Public Health at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill, confirmed that the beginning of the end of US elimination was January 20, 2025, in Texas —that date was included in the letter PAHO sent to the US informing it of the loss of elimination status. That Texas outbreak was declared over on August 18, 2025, after 762 cases were confirmed in the state. But the virus carried on elsewhere and is still simmering.
“Since January 20, 2025, the US, Canada, and Mexico have been passing measles cases back and forth across borders,” Brewer said, and the national data shows multiple, “genetically distinct” measles introductions into the US. “However, there is one genomic lineage that predominates across the cases and ties many of them, the majority of them, together,” he said.
For people closely tracking the US measles status, a key question has been whether the big outbreaks that followed the initial one in Texas were clearly linked. If they were, it would be immediately obvious that the US had lost the elimination status; but if not, and the outbreaks were driven by different virus introductions, the US could have kept its measles-free status based on the technicality of how the status is defined.
Data that might hold the answer to this question has been elusive. The measles strain in Texas, D8-9171, appeared similar to the viruses seen subsequently in big outbreaks in Arizona and Utah . But the strain was also similar to those from Mexico and Canada. Generally, there can be relatively small genetic changes among measles viruses, and genetic data alone is not used by PAHO to evaluate elimination. In June, ProPublica tried to get at the answer itself, conducting its own genetic analysis of measles strains in the US. It concluded that “the measles virus still spreading in Utah as of this May is very closely related to the one that sickened Texans over a year ago.” But the outlet acknowledged this wasn’t a “smoking gun.”
To date, the question lingers. Brewer cannot yet explicitly disclose what the NSC reported to the PAHO about possible links between the Texas outbreak and any of the subsequent large outbreaks in 2025. That includes the one in nearby Utah or one in South Carolina, which began in October 2025 and ultimately tallied 997 cases by the time it was declared over in April 2026.
For its part, the PAHO did not respond to multiple requests for comment from Ars Technica on linkages between the outbreaks.
But in a twist, Brewer noted that the answer to the question might be moot; the lineage that started in Texas on January 20 might not be the only one that has been sustained and could have lost the country its status. There are “one or two that have gone on for more than 12 months,” he said.
With the designation now formally lost, health and medical experts are coming to grips with the reality that measles is once again endemic in the US. Details of how the US should move forward are up for debate; the US is now required to submit a “corrective action plan” to the PAHO, outlining how the country intends to regain its elimination status. But the fundamental solution is obvious and straightforward: The US needs to increase vaccination rates.
While the virus has been raging in religious communities with low vaccination rates, the entire US has seen slipping vaccination coverage. That makes it easier for the virus to gain a foothold virtually anywhere.
A protective vaccination rate is considered to be 95 percent; according to the latest data , only 92.4 percent of kindergartners were vaccinated with the measles, mumps, and rubella (MMR) vaccine in the 2025–2026 school year. Real-time forecasting, anomaly detection, and optimization, powered by IBM time-series models with more than 50 million downloads. Now available natively on Confluent, in the cloud and on premises, running on CPUs.
Every business generates a continuous record of change: a machine reading, a payment, a sale, an order, or a change in inventory. These observations form time series, and they carry signals that can help teams anticipate what happens next.
The challenge is turning those signals into decisions while they still matter. A forecast delivered after a production run, a stockout, or a payment authorization may be accurate, but too late to influence the outcome.
IBM and Confluent are bringing time-series foundation models closer to the data as it flows. With Apache Flink, teams can apply forecasting , anomaly detection and semantic intelligence to streaming data using SQL, making model outputs available to the applications and people responsible for the next action.
Foundation models have changed how organizations work with text, images, and documents. Time-series foundation models extend a similar idea to numerical data by learning general patterns from diverse historical data and then applying that knowledge to new series and tasks. The models can provide a starting point without requiring teams to train a separate model for every series. Depending on the task and deployment, teams can also fine-tune a model or combine its outputs with other data and business logic.
Figure 1. More than 50 million downloads, and the family of four models behind them
Now the time series foundation models run natively inside Confluent as built-in functions in the cloud and on premises. In Confluent Cloud they are fully managed, with nothing to deploy ( documentation ). On premises, the models can run within your own infrastructure using Confluent Platform for Apache Flink.( documentation ). The models run on CPUs, without requiring GPUs.
The models can support a range of mission-critical use cases, from helping keep production lines in spec and detecting unusual store activity to improving product-level planning. They can also provide signals to assess card payments and forecast trading volume to help place large orders. These building blocks can be applied across manufacturing, retail, banking, and airlines, bringing insights closer to where decisions are made.
See how time series and real-time context come together to create value:
Businesses operate continuously. Orders are updated, payments arrive, shipments are delayed, and inventory changes throughout the day. Yet the information behind these events often sits across systems that update at different times or rely on periodic batch processes. When applications and AI agents act on outdated or inconsistent information, they risk making decisions that no longer reflect what is happening.
A Streamhouse addresses this by continuously capturing, processing, governing, and serving current business context. Confluent’s Data Streaming Platform brings together five capabilities—connect, stream, process, govern, and query—to make that context available to applications, analytics, and agents. Apache Flink transforms and enriches data as it flows, while Lightning Tables provide low-latency access to the current state.
Figure 2. The Streamhouse on Confluent: from existing data sources to current business context that agents, applications, analytics and lakehouses use anywhere.
Time-series models add predictive power to this architecture. Flink can prepare the data, invoke forecasting and anomaly detection, and make the results available alongside the events that produced them. Other models—including large language models, statistical models, and specialized machine learning systems—can contribute where appropriate.
Figure 3. The intelligence layer of the Streamhouse: time series models, large language models, and ML and statistical models, with orchestration across them.
- Scale model development . A pretrained model can provide a common starting point across many time series, reducing the need to develop and maintain a separate model for each one.
- Refresh predictions as data changes . Forecasts can incorporate recent observations as part of a streaming workflow, subject to the model’s requirements and the pipeline’s configuration.
- Put signals closer to decisions . Forecasts and anomalies can be routed to operational applications sooner, where teams can combine them with business context, rules, and human judgment.
- Run compact models on CPUs. The models are small enough to run on standard CPUs alongside the streaming pipeline, in the cloud or on premises, which can reduce the need for dedicated GPU infrastructure and simplify deployment.
Figure 4. Stream native time-series intelligence on Confluent
The following scenarios illustrate how organizations could combine time-series models, streaming data, and application logic.
An ice cream line’s quality depends on overrun—the amount of air whipped into the mix. Today, the process engineer and operator rely on QA lab measurements taken after the tubs are filled. If a new cream lot or a warm, humid day changes the process, hours of production may already need rework by the time the team sees the result.
To get ahead of the problem, a pretrained TTM model reads SCADA telemetry and QA measurements every 10 minutes. It forecasts the share of tubs expected to be in spec four hours ahead, along with a likely range.
When the forecast falls below the plant’s target, an optimization process evaluates combinations of freezer draw temperature and airflow. Because the model takes these control variables as inputs, it can score each option before anything changes on the line. The operator approves the recommended setpoints, while routine adjustments can be automated within predefined guardrails.
The outcome is a more proactive process: less rework, lower energy use per tonne, and more consistent quality. The same approach can be applied to ovens, dryers, kilns, and mills.
Figure 5. A forecast of product quality helps the operator evaluate freezer setpoints before making an adjustment.
A store operations team monitors sales for thousands of products across hundreds of stores. Fixed thresholds often flag predictable weekend peaks while missing quieter changes, such as a product selling less than expected. As alerts accumulate, it becomes harder for the team to know where to focus.
AI_DETECT_ANOMALIES gives each sales series an expected range based on its recent history. Each new reading is compared with that range at a confidence level the team chooses, without training a separate model for every product and store.
When sales fall outside the expected range, the signal can be combined with inventory and store data to help identify a likely cause and recommend a next step—for example, checking the shelf or replenishing stock. The same approach can be applied to machine sensors, API telemetry, meter readings, and payment volumes.
Figure 6. Store sales are compared with an expected range. In the view shown, recurring peaks remain within the range and no anomaly is flagged.
A category planner and a replenishment team need to keep products available across every store without carrying excess inventory. But forecasts may be refreshed only once a week, often focusing on top-selling products, while the long tail is managed with simpler rules.
